title: Certificate Holdings and the Episode Ceiling on Personal Checking Goodwill Relief
content:
Two cases raise the episode ceiling that holds down goodwill relief on a Personal Checking account, read from the owner's certificate principal held under Certificates of Deposit, from card payments under Personal Credit Cards and from a premier money market balance held under Savings & Money Market Accounts.

- Where the owner's certificate principal is above zero **and** the owner has made at least 6 card payments in the last twelve months, the episode ceiling is a wide episode ceiling of 400.00.
- Where the case above does not apply **and** either the certificate principal reaches the certificate relationship minimum of 25000.00 **or** the premier money market balance reaches the protection source minimum of 5000.00, it is a standard episode ceiling of 250.00.
- Where neither case applies, neither of those ceilings is used.

**Worked ceilings on hypothetical inputs.**

| Owner's position | Episode ceiling |
|---|---|
| Certificate principal of 900.00, 7 card payments in the last twelve months | 400.00 |
| Certificate principal of 30000.00, 2 card payments | 250.00 |
| No certificate principal, premier money market balance of 9000.00 | 250.00 |
| No certificate principal, premier money market balance of 100.00 | Neither ceiling is used |

Any certificate principal above zero satisfies the first limb of the first case, but the card payment limb must hold alongside it. The second case is met by either of its limbs alone, and equality satisfies each threshold.
